summary: Pittsburg, NH summit tower: 1911 first lookout, 1933 steel tower, closed 1976. Steel frame remains with cab and steps gone; climbing unsafe; reached on foot.

facts.design: Steel tower dating to 1933; cab removed, steel frame remains
facts.status_note: The steel frame stands, but the cab and steps are gone and it is no longer a working lookout.

access.note: Wooden steps removed to discourage climbing; the trail guide calls the structure unsafe. Reached on foot by a hiking trail.

visit.trail_note: Hiking trail follows a brook to the summit, where the tower remains

facts.agency: New Hampshire Department of Natural and Cultural Resources

events.note: First tower on the site, built by the New Hampshire Timberland Owners Association
State took control of the site and built a 30-foot wooden tower
Replaced by the current steel structure; the NHLR Built field gives 1933
Closed; NHLR says the cab was later removed
FFLA says the state burned the cab around 1985, and the stairs and landings at the same time. NHLR and Trail Finder say the cab was removed instead.

notes_for_editor: Cab fate conflicts: NHLR says the cab was later removed and Trail Finder says it was removed once out of use, while FFLA says the state burned it around 1985. Stairs: FFLA says burned, Trail Finder says removed to discourage climbing. The story reports both. NH Family Hikes lists a 'North Deer Mountain' in Pittsburg whose stairs were removed; it may be this tower, but I did not use it because the name match is not certain. onlyinyourstate.com returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The rehabilitation status is only as of the 2023 FFLA report; no later news was found. The access level 'restricted' is my reading: the wooden steps were removed to discourage climbing (trail guide), and no source says the tower is formally closed to climbing, so the story no longer says it is. The steps are cited to FFLA and the trail guide, since NHLR does not mention them. No photos added.
